title: Historic/dead faith cannot justify—James and Galatians
source_text: V. Porro fides illa mortua, iners, & otiosa, quam Protestantes historicam vocant, justificare non potest. Nam diserte docet Jacobus ejusmodi reperiri posse in ipsis Daemonibus, illamque ad salutem, adeoque ad justitiam consequendam nihil prodesse. Quid proderit, inquit, fratres mei, si fidem dicat aliquis se habere, opera autem non habeat? numquid poterit fides salvare eum? Jac. 2. v. 14. Et postea, Tu credis Deum unum esse; bene facis: & Daemones credunt, & contremiscunt. v. 19. Unde est quod Paulus, scribens ad Galatas, affirmat nihil in Christo valere, nisi fidem quae per dilectionem operatur: & per consequens fidem ipsam, nisi per dilectionem operetur, eorum in numero esse quae nihil in Christo valent. Nam, inquit, in Christo Jesu neque circumcisio aliquid valet, neque praeputium, sed fides quae per charitatem operatur. Gal. 5. v. 6. Ac ne quis in eo fallatur, & charitate ac bonis operibus vacuus, fidei cujusdam inertis & otiosae nomine sibi blandiatur, aliis in locis eandem sententiam repetens, pro fide quae per charitatem operatur, modo novam creaturam, modo observationem mandatorum Dei substituit. Sic enim idem Apostolus, epistolae jam citatae cap. 6. commate 15. loquitur, In Christo Jesu neque circumcisio aliquid valet, neque praeputium, sed nova creatura. Et 1 Cor. 7. v. 19. Circumcisio nihil est, & praeputium nihil est, sed observatio mandatorum Dei. Ita ut Apostolo haec tria sint aequivalentia, Observatio mandatorum Dei, Nova creatura, & Fides per charitatem operans.
pass_a_gloss: Further, that dead, inert, and idle faith which Protestants call historic cannot justify. For James expressly teaches that such can be found even in the demons themselves, and that it profits nothing toward salvation and so toward obtaining righteousness. What does it profit, he says, my brothers, if someone says he has faith but does not have works? Can faith save him? (Jas 2:14). And afterward: You believe that God is one; you do well: and the demons believe and shudder (v. 19). Hence Paul, writing to the Galatians, affirms that nothing avails in Christ except faith that works through love; and consequently faith itself, unless it works through love, is among the things that avail nothing in Christ. For, he says, in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision avails anything, but faith working through charity (Gal 5:6). And lest anyone be deceived and, empty of charity and good works, flatter himself with the name of some inert and idle faith, in other places repeating the same sense he substitutes now a new creature, now the keeping of God's commandments, for faith that works through charity. So the same Apostle in the letter already cited, chapter 6 verse 15, says: In Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision avails anything, but a new creation. And 1 Cor 7:19: Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing, but keeping the commandments of God. So that for the Apostle these three are equivalent: Keeping God's commandments, A new creation, and Faith working through charity.
pass_b_english: Historic/dead faith—possible even in demons—cannot justify.
Paul equates justifying faith with love-working faith, new creation, and obedience.

choices.why: Protestant label for bare doctrinal assent.
